reason: Retains all nontrivial independent-normal affine-sum laws and the corrected bivariate density, moments, correlation and zero-correlation independence. Does not assert the canonical general non-implication from uncorrelated normal marginals to independence. The positive component variances match the book's definition of a normal law.

Retains the general L2 MSE decomposition and unique minimizer, the fair-coin mean and variance, all specified loss values, and the factor-two algebra. Omits the explicit first-order derivative calculation and verification of the actual plotted curve. L2 is the standing finiteness convention, not an extra restriction.

The normalized three-point weights and all three vectors are exactly the canonical counterexample, including positive variances, both correlations, almost-sure equalities and failure of every everywhere-affine representation. Finite weighted sums are ordinary expectations for this displayed PMF.

Exactly the bounded-correlation theorem and both positive-slope almost-sure affine equivalences. L2 and positive variances express the standing moment assumptions and the domain of correlation; no conclusion is assumed.

Retains the first partial derivatives, normal equations and unique risk minimum for arbitrary L2 X,Y with positive regressor variance. Omits joint differentiability on R^2 and the zero-variance case. Places the Hessian-value identities, CEF approximation, residual identities and linear-CEF conclusion behind a supplied square-integrable conditional mean; does not assert existence of such a version. The iterated deriv equalities do not separately certify second differentiability.

Retains canonical counterexample (a): the two equal-weight outcomes give distinct predictors with equal covariance and MSE zero and one. This genuinely refutes uniqueness of an affine predictor from the covariance equation. Omits counterexample (b) and the general affine-covariance identity.

Exactly characterizes the covariance equation alone by the slope and the covariance-plus-mean equations by the BLP coefficients, and explicitly supplies unique risk minimality. L2 and positive regressor variance match the full canonical claim.

The uniform density is exactly the stated U(0,1) law, the noise is an independent N(0,1), and the response, conditional-mean version, moments and unique affine optimum are the canonical ones. The event-integral conditional-mean predicate correctly renders a version as permitted by the standing assumptions.

Correct covariance entries, symmetry, variance diagonal and the full variance-of-sum identity, with all coordinate pairs quantified. Fin K is arbitrary, including every positive dimension; the allowed zero dimension does not make the statement vacuous. Coordinate L2 is the standing finite-moment convention.

The explicit affine function has its intercept at zero, each slope as the unit coordinate increment, and actual coordinate derivatives equal to the slope. This is precisely the canonical formal content, stated for every affine coefficient vector, hence including BLP coefficients.

Retains the general equal-probability finite-population PMF and moments, the complete four-unit example, the corrected minus-sign variance identity and the precise discrepancy of the printed plus sign, and empirical-law mean and variance identities for every positive sample size. Using measure integrals gives the canonical dF integrals.

Retains exactly the eventual-probability-level equivalence with 0 <= p < 1 and correct quantifier order. Omits a separate complementary-good-event limit equivalence and an explicit instance showing failure at p=1.

Exactly the measurable-set indicator-expectation identity and consistency of every fixed empirical CDF ordinate under IID sampling, including degenerate ordinates. Measurability of the set D is correctly imposed.

Certifies the normalized PMF weights and exact finite first and second moments, strictly positive variance arithmetic, and divergent nonnegative fourth-moment sum. Omits a measure-space realization, IID draws, and an explicit statement that the variance of the squares is not finite. It does not refute the true sample-variance consistency conclusion.

States both exact expectation and full consistency conclusions under IID sampling and finite positive variance, without any fourth-moment assumption. Does not state the general integrable-variable WLLN or the intermediate sample-mean and sample-second-moment limits included in the canonical corrected-proof text.

Correctly restores the estimated random sequence in both definitions and both centered formulations, and proves equivalence of variance and standard-error consistency. Nonnegative estimates are the real-square-root domain condition; an L2 limiting law expresses the standing finite-variance convention. No positive limiting variance or Gaussian law is silently imposed.

Retains the constant-functional derivative and exclusion of every positive-variance Gaussian limit, and the quadratic Bernoulli functional's differentiability, value at F, exact second moment and probability-zero limit. Omits the explicit CDF comparison at zero, boundedness/nonconstancy of the quadratic functional, F(0)=1/2, identification of its derivative, the binomial law, scalar formula convergence, and construction of IID draws. The constant-functional portion still refutes the printed theorem under its positive-variance definition of asymptotic normality.

Retains the positive-variance functional-delta conclusion and also concludes outer weak convergence of the empirical CDF process. Quantifies over a supplied Borel probability bridge with the displayed tangent support and all finite-dimensional Gaussian laws, measurable scalar plug-ins, and an L2 derivative image with positive variance. Does not assert bridge existence or the possibly degenerate alternative. The bridge hypotheses specify a law, not the empirical-process convergence conclusion; the Bernoulli rank-one bridge gives a nondegenerate instance.
